case_studies.title: An Irish accountancy firm's AI & Automation service line, built from zero, with its client platform live in 10 days
case_studies.summary: An Irish chartered accountancy and audit firm offered no AI. Adrian built the service line and runs it: a 20-module client platform live in 10 days, EU-only AI processing enforced in code, an AML gate, Irish statute as software, and AI training for the whole firm.
case_studies.client: M.A. Whately & Co., Irish chartered accountancy and audit firm
case_studies.role: Director of AI & Business Automation (contractor). Sole owner of AI at the firm, reporting to the principal: scoping, pricing, build, training and support.
case_studies.timeline: Service line from October 2025. Platform: first build 23 Sep 2026, live 3 Oct 2026, current scope by 21 Oct 2026
case_studies.problem: Build software a regulated profession can put its name on, fast, without an in-house engineering team. Client financial data, identity numbers and bank details are involved, so data residency, tenant isolation, AML checks and GDPR retention had to exist from the first release, not be retrofitted.
built: 20 product modules (16 client-facing, 4 practice-only): bills and receipts, VAT, supplier payments, credit control, Irish tax deadlines, proposals with a fee calculator, expenses, a client portal. 53 request templates across 14 sectors.

AI bills reader. Two Gemini models via Vertex AI EU reach a consensus on every field, with Claude as an opt-in fallback. VAT numbers are checked against VIES, bills post to Xero, and supplier payments export as SEPA pain.001 files.

Irish statute as software. Revenue deadlines for PAYE, RCT, VAT, Form 46G, LPT and Form 11, CRO audit-exemption tests (S.I. 301/2024), statutory late-payment interest and Irish bank holidays, encoded as rules and covered by tests.
An AML gate. Client account set-up stays blocked until the identity check is verified. IBAN confirmations are admin-only, stamped and audited by a database trigger.

AI assistant with confirm-first actions. A tool-registry agent that runs under the user's own session permissions, proposes an action, and executes only after the user confirms. Per-tenant cost caps. A daily staff brief went live on 7 Oct.

Numbers computed, words generated. The fee engine computes every figure deterministically and lets AI compose only the wording, a rule written down with reference to model non-determinism and Irish DPC guidance.
Security by default. Row-level tenant isolation, CSP and HSTS, masked PPS and IBAN numbers, 192-bit recipient tokens, an audit log and automatic retention purge. SSL Labs grade A.

A service the firm can sell. A five-tier price ladder (Free, Essentials, Pro, Business and Practice Bookkeeping) with add-ons, and an AI for Accountants session that trained the full team (10+ people) with live demos, backed by an AI Academy of 8 lessons and 48 prompts.
results: 10 days: from first commit (23 Sep) to live production (3 Oct 2026)
20: modules live within four weeks
99.8%: field accuracy of the AI bills reader (428 of 429 fields) on a 64-file synthetic test corpus; 97.6% on the browser path, up from 86.7%, with 0 silent errors
< 1 cent: per document, about USD 0.009 per scan
3,000+: automated checks green (3,230 with 0 failures on 17 Oct)
87/87: deploy smoke test on every deploy since 6 Oct (85/85 at launch)
10+: people trained: the full firm team, in an AI for Accountants session with live demos

case_studies.title: HubSpot to Xero invoicing across 3 legal entities and 4 currencies
case_studies.summary: Automation that moves real money: closed deals become approved Xero invoices in the right legal entity and currency, emailed to the customer and chased until paid. Live since April 2026, about 52 invoices a month under signed approvals.
case_studies.client: Multi-entity B2B software reseller (US, UK and EU companies), delivered through M.A. Whately & Co.
case_studies.timeline: Designed February 2026, live 15 April 2026, hardening release 15 September 2026
case_studies.problem: Turn every Closed Won deal into a correct draft invoice in the right Xero organisation and currency, route it through finance approval, email the customer without landing in spam, and chase payment, without anyone re-keying a deal.
built: Eight n8n workflows, 119 nodes: a router, a deal-bundle fetcher, a transformer, a Xero draft creator, an approval watcher, payment reminders, a retry queue and a global error handler.
Signed approvals. Finance approves through HMAC-signed links; the watcher verifies the signature before anything is sent.
Idempotency and a dead-letter queue. State lives in Supabase, every write is keyed, and failed jobs retry up to five times before landing in a queue a human reviews.
Customer email via the company's own mailbox rather than the ledger's mailer, to stay out of spam folders. Reminders at 7 days before, on the due date, and 14 days overdue.
results: 212+: invoices processed by September 2026 (about 52 a month)
3: Xero organisations and 4 currencies from one CRM
9: bugs found and fixed in a pre-launch audit (2 critical), plus 18 edge cases covered and a 15-item go-live checklist
USD 4-7K: estimated payment fees avoided in the first five months (estimate; rates not independently verified)

case_studies.title: An EU-sovereign, multi-tenant financial reporting platform for the education sector
case_studies.summary: An EU-sovereign financial reporting platform with no US-owned service in the stack: self-hosted in the Netherlands, Microsoft sign-in, Exact Online ledgers turned into board-ready reports for education organisations, and tenant isolation proven by tests.

headline.label: isolation policies caught by mutation tests

case_studies.role: Architect and builder. Hourly and fixed-price phases.
case_studies.timeline: Infrastructure from August 2026, reporting checked live 16 October 2026, collaboration workspace in build
case_studies.status: Reporting checked live on demo data; next module in build
case_studies.problem: Many organisations on one platform, each seeing only its own numbers, with infrastructure that stays in the EU and under the client's control. A data leak between tenants would end the product.
built: A regulated pilot, designed up front. Adrian designed the pilot across three organisation types (a bookkeeping firm, an audit firm and school boards), raised the need for a data processing agreement per firm before anyone asked, and wrote the security brief for their IT teams. Both firms approved.

Self-hosted core on a Dutch VPS with Docker Compose: Supabase (PostgreSQL with row-level security), n8n, Caddy for TLS, encrypted off-site backups, ledger tokens encrypted at rest and secrets kept encrypted.
Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on bridged into the database's own session tokens, so the isolation rules apply to every query.
Exact Online sync (read-only) on a schedule, and a report builder driven by the client's own chart-of-accounts workbook, so finance stays the source of truth for structure.
Reporting: profit and loss, balance sheet and cash flow with drill-down to ledger transactions, per-tenant branding, and a plain-language AI explainer clearly labelled as beta.
results: 52/52: sign-in end-to-end tests, including link reuse, expiry, replay and a five-strike lockout

case_studies.title: Daily revenue reporting for a 5-hotel group, matched to the accountants cell by cell
case_studies.summary: Six daily reports for five hotels, built from the property-management and point-of-sale exports and matched to the accounting team's own figures, cell by cell, for every hotel.

headline.label: matched to accounting, cell by cell

case_studies.client: Hospitality group operating in Spain and Romania
case_studies.status: Delivered, with a cloud pipeline for daily runs
case_studies.problem: Produce the six daily reports automatically, and make them match what the accountants would have produced, down to each cell. A report that is close is not a report finance can use.
built: Source rules agreed with the accountants line by line: which export feeds each row, what is excluded, and which values they still fill by hand.
